messages.parties.help.m1:
§6§m----------------------------------------§r
§6✦ §e§lParties§r §8» §7Form teams, track live stats, and share §6XP§7.
§7Press §6[%s§6]§7 to open the menu button & edit your layout.
§8» §fClick a tutorial below for more information:§r
tutorial.parties.alt_1: After pressing the §e'Show Mouse'§f keybind, your mouse becomes visible, and the §emenu button appears§f.
tutorial.parties.alt_2: Clicking it §ereveals a menu§f with two other buttons: A §6HUD Layout Editor§f and a §6Template Editor§f.
tutorial.parties.alt_3: Let's start with the §6HUD Layout Editor§f.
tutorial.parties.alt_4: This editor allows you to §emodify§f each frame's §3position, template, and anchoring§f to match your needs.
tutorial.parties.alt_5: §eClick§f to §3customize§f any frame, or §edrag§f to §3reposition§f it. The highlighted one right here is your §2Player Frame§f.
tutorial.parties.alt_6: And here is your §2Party Frame§f. If you aren't in a group yet, §esample teammates§f are displayed so you can adjust the complete layout.
tutorial.parties.alt_7: And this is where you §eedit§f the §3properties§f of each frame. The §ename§f of the §3selected frame§f is shown here as well.
tutorial.parties.alt_8: If the editor gets in the way of your frame positioning, this button allows you to §2move the entire editor§f to the §etop§f of the screen.
tutorial.parties.alt_9: View the current §3position§f (relative to the §6Anchor§f) and §3scale§f here. You can §edrag the frame§f directly to change its §3position§f, and §euse the arrow buttons§f to §3change the scale§f.
tutorial.parties.alt_10: Choose a §6customized template§f for the §3selected frame§f here. In the pop-up window you can §5view the template directory§f and §2modify the template's properties§f as well.
tutorial.parties.alt_11: These buttons let you §edisable§f the grid (and extra outlines), as well as §ereset§f the current frame's §3scale, position, and anchor§f to its §4default values§f.
tutorial.parties.alt_12: Pick an anchor point here so your frame §3scales and snaps§f into place on §2any screen size§f. §eShift-click§f to §3change the anchor§f while keeping the frame §2right where it is§f.
tutorial.parties.alt_13: Let's look at the §6Template Editor§f now.
tutorial.parties.editor_1: This is the §6Template Editor§f. It provides deep customization of every element for §2very unique templates§f.
tutorial.parties.editor_2: This area contains §3properties§f like §escale, position, and size§f that are related to each element. You can §etoggle the visibility§f of each element here as well.
tutorial.parties.editor_3: And this shows the list of all elements, §eexpandable§f by the button above. §3There may also be §chidden elements§3 from supporting mods if they aren't installed.
tutorial.parties.editor_4: If the transparent background makes things hard to see, you can toggle the display to use §etextures§f instead with this button. §2It will be turned on for the rest of the tutorial so you can see how it looks like!
tutorial.parties.editor_5: These editor buttons §ecome in pairs§f: the left applies to all elements, while the right applies to the selected one. You can §crevert to default (left)§f, §3restore your last save (center)§f, or §6undo and redo (right)§f.
tutorial.parties.editor_6: The §6Layout element§f handles frame size and extra padding options for whenever the frame contains multiple players or mobs, like the §2Party Frame§f.
tutorial.parties.editor_7: That’s why §ethree preview entries§f appear instead of one when it is selected so you can see how your §6Padding Settings§f would look like in a multi-entry frame.
tutorial.parties.editor_8: This is the §6Stage View§f, where you can drag and zoom the UI with your mouse for precise editing of each element.
tutorial.parties.editor_9: This is the §6View Menu§f, where you can toggle the grid, lock dragging, center the view, change the amount of stacking players shown, freeze animations, or make all element animations play at once.
tutorial.parties.editor_10: This is the §6Main Editor Menu§f. §3Load, import, §2save, or export§f your templates here. To use a preset, §2save it §ffirst, then §eattach it §fto a frame in the §6HUD Layout Editor§f or the §6Linking Menu§f next to it. Click to expand or minimize.
tutorial.parties.editor_11: This is the §6Linking Menu§f. Click to §eattach this template §fto a frame, or §cunlink §fit to restore defaults. A §3cyan accent §fshows an active link, while §7gray §fmeans unlinked. Click to expand or minimize.
tutorial.parties.title: Party Guide
tutorial.parties.general.subtitle: §eRPG Party System & Team UI
tutorial.parties.general.description: §2Gather your party and conquer your world together! §6Parties §7upgrades team play with §3modular party frames§7, §3deep config options§7, §3native mod support§7, and §3custom HUD layouts §7you can §3build §7and §3share §7with friends or bundle in a modpack. §eRead on for more details!
tutorial.parties.general.lost_prompt: §4Lost? §7Don't worry! Here are some §2tutorials§7 to help you understand how to configure the mod.
tutorial.parties.general.highlight.hud: §e• §6Fully Customizable HUD: §7Move, scale, toggle, and customize player and party frames.
tutorial.parties.general.highlight.templ: §e• §6Template Sharing: §7Export and import custom templates via files or character strings.
tutorial.parties.general.highlight.dynam: §e• §6Party Dynamics: §7Adds XP sharing, friendly-fire protection, spell tagging, location tracking, and more.
tutorial.parties.general.highlight.compa: §e• §6Mod Compatibility: §7Integrated support for several popular mods, with more to come!
tutorial.parties.features.description: Whether you play alone or with friends, Parties lets you customize your interface to match your style. From various HUD settings to built-in party mechanics, here is everything included in the mod so far:
tutorial.parties.feature.tutorial.title: In-Game Tutorial
tutorial.parties.feature.tutorial.desc: The /party help menu has been completely overhauled with a new informational window. It features clear guides on templates, frame and party settings, plus visual tutorial sequences to help you get started.
tutorial.parties.feature.hud_editor.desc: Move, scale, anchor, and toggle party or player frames on the fly. Includes grid snapping, alignment guides, and a live preview while you edit.
tutorial.parties.feature.template_creato: Build your own UI templates from scratch. Export setups directly into shareable strings or JSON files to drop into modpacks or send to friends.
tutorial.parties.feature.modded_elements: Shows resource bars from other magic mods automatically, including Iron's Spells cast and mana bars, Ars Nouveau mana, and more, all of which can be customized extensively.
tutorial.parties.feature.player_tracking: Keep tabs on teammates across long distances and dimensions. Party avatars also function as a built-in compass radar, or you can use on-screen edge markers to see where allies are around you.
tutorial.parties.feature.xp_sharing.desc: Splits mob XP with nearby party members. Keeps leveling fair during mob farms or dungeon crawls, so supportive and ranged roles don't fall behind.
tutorial.parties.feature.friendly_fire.d: Stops accidental friendly fire from happening ever again! Protects teammates, pets, summons, leashed mobs, and other damage hits from stray swings.
tutorial.parties.feature.spell_tagging.d: Keeps offensive spells from locking onto teammates with a new Hostile Spell tag. Attacks, projectiles, and hostile status effects won't affect allies while friendly fire is turned off.
tutorial.parties.commands.description: §7These are all the commands currently available for the §3Parties §7mod. Do note that the §e/parties§7 prefix can be replaced with §e/p§7 and §e/party§7.
tutorial.parties.command.invite.desc: §7Sends a party invite to a player. Invites expire after 60 seconds.
tutorial.parties.command.accept.desc: §7Accepts a party invite from a player. If receiving an invitation, you can also click on the respective chat link.
tutorial.parties.command.decline.desc: §7Declines the last party invite from a player. Clicking on the respective chat link also allows you to decline a specific invitation as well.
tutorial.parties.command.disband.desc: §7Disbands the party you're currently in. Can only be done by the party leader.
tutorial.parties.command.kick.desc: §7Removes a player from your current party. If no other players were to remain, it disbands the party instead. Can only be done by the party leader.
tutorial.parties.command.leave.desc: §7Leaves your current party. If leader, it passes leadership to someone else. If party would be left with one player, the party disbands instead.
tutorial.parties.command.promote.desc: §7Transfers leadership to another player. If the leader is offline, leadership may automatically be transferred depending on settings in parties-common.toml.
tutorial.parties.command.help.desc: §7Provides very detailed information on how the party system and hud editor works. Brings up a window that shows several informational tabs along with launching several tutorial sequences.
tutorial.parties.roadmap.description: §7These are all the integrations §5planned§7, §ebeing worked on§7, and §aimplemented§7 since 2.0.0:
tutorial.parties.roadmap.irons_spells.de: §7Cast Bar, Mana Bar and friendly-fire spell and summon support.
tutorial.parties.roadmap.ars_nouveau.des: §7Mana Bar, friendly-fire summon and familiar support.
tutorial.parties.roadmap.xaeros.title: §eXaero's Minimap
tutorial.parties.roadmap.xaeros.desc: §7Minimap UI integration, party tracking, map syncing(?)
tutorial.parties.roadmap.epic_fight.desc: §7Stamina bar element, considering cast/skill bar integration.
tutorial.parties.roadmap.voice_chat.desc: §7Voice Chat status border, party synchronization, and automatic group creation.
tutorial.parties.roadmap.ftb_teams.title: §5FTB Teams
tutorial.parties.roadmap.open_pac.title: §5Open Parties and Claims
tutorial.parties.roadmap.jeed.title: §5Just Enough Effect Descriptions

§6Platform & Version Notes:
§8• §eFabric: §7Currently Forge and NeoForge only; Fabric is planned for future updates.
§8• §eBackports: §7No backports planned; development targets modern releases first. After the in-progress mod support is added, a port to 1.21.1 will be released.
